topic.subject: chemistry
topic.title: Conservation of mass and balanced equations
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: Mass and Equations; TGS 2026-27: conservation and balancing
topic.overview: In a chemical reaction atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed. A balanced symbol equation therefore contains the same number of each type of atom on both sides.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Reactants are written before the arrow and products after it.
The arrow means 'reacts to form'; it is not an equals sign in a mechanism.
Balance equations by changing whole-number coefficients in front of formulae, never by changing subscripts.
In a closed system total mass stays constant because all substances, including gases, remain included.
An apparent mass decrease in an open system can occur when gas escapes; an increase can occur when oxygen from air is added.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a starting substance in a chemical reaction
a substance formed by a chemical reaction
a number placed before a formula to multiply the whole formula
an equation with equal numbers of each type of atom on both sides
total mass remains constant because atoms are not created or destroyed
a system in which matter cannot enter or leave
a system in which matter such as gas can enter or leave
a process in which atoms are rearranged into new substances

workedExamples.working: Use coefficients to give four H and two O atoms on both sides.

workedExamples.prompt: 10.0 g reactants react in a sealed flask. Predict total product mass.
workedExamples.working: Mass is conserved in the closed system.

practicals.title: Conservation in a sealed system
practicals.aim: Test mass before and after a reaction that produces gas.
practicals.variables: IV may be reaction stage; DV is total mass; keep quantities and apparatus constant.
practicals.method: Place reactants in a sealed flask or zip bag, measure total mass, mix without opening, then remeasure.
practicals.expectedResult: Total mass should remain the same within measurement uncertainty.
practicals.safety: Use small quantities, eye protection and a container that can safely withstand gas production.
practicals.evaluation: Use a more precise balance, repeat and check the seal if mass appears to change.

commonMistakes: Changing H2O into H2O2 to balance oxygen.
Forgetting that a coefficient multiplies every atom in a formula.
Saying mass disappears when a gas leaves an open container.
examTips: Count each element on both sides in a tally.
Balance one element at a time and recheck all elements.
For mass questions, first ask whether the system is open or closed.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.aim: Test mass before and after a reaction that produces gas.
practicals.variables: IV may be reaction stage; DV is total mass; keep quantities and apparatus constant.
practicals.method: Place reactants in a sealed flask or zip bag, measure total mass, mix without opening, then remeasure.
practicals.expectedResult: Total mass should remain the same within measurement uncertainty.
practicals.safety: Use small quantities, eye protection and a container that can safely withstand gas production.
practicals.evaluation: Use a more precise balance, repeat and check the seal if mass appears to change.
